topics.title: Getting Started
topics.body:
1. Choose a supported installation with **Find games...** or **Browse folder...**.
2. Select the installation explicitly. The editor starts with no active game.
3. Choose the required **Active Variant**: Elvira I VGA, Elvira I EGA, or Elvira II VGA.
4. Choose an **Edition**: Original (EN) is read-only; SK/S1-style editions own isolated editable project state.
5. Make edits in Graphics, Game Text, Runtime UI, or Font, then use **Save to project**. This does not modify the pristine game and does not create runnable files. Text and Graphics edits are materialized by a later variant build; saved Font and Runtime UI overrides are validated project state but are NOT materialized by Build variant in v1.0.
6. Use **Build variant...** to open the active Runtime + Edition build target, build/rebuild it, review its manifest/readiness, and only then use **Run** or **Debug**. Font overrides use the explicit standalone Apply-to-EXE workflow where supported, not the variant build.

For exported sprite PNG files, avoid Microsoft Paint because it may turn transparent pixels opaque white; use an RGBA-preserving editor such as FireAlpaca, Paint.NET, or GIMP. Changing the interface language never activates, builds, runs, or modifies a game.

topics.title: Active Variant
topics.body:
**Installation** and **Active Variant** are separate choices. Elvira I provides **VGA / RUNVGA** and **EGA / RUNEGA**. Elvira II provides **VGA / RUNIT**.

Changing the active variant updates the context used by Graphics, Game Text, Runtime UI, Font, and Mods/Launcher. Selecting a variant does not build files and does not start the game.

topics.title: Variant Manager
topics.body:
Variant Manager shows the supported runtime variants, their editor-owned output directory, ownership state, build state, and launch readiness.

Use it to see whether an output is missing, incomplete, ready, or unsafe. A directory that is foreign, invalid, or not owned by the editor is reported and preserved; it must never be silently adopted or deleted.

topics.title: Build Status
topics.body:
**Missing** — the editor-owned variant output does not exist.

**Invalid** — the current context or output directory is not valid for a safe build.

**Incomplete** — an owned output exists but required build products are missing or incomplete.

**Ready** — the owned output contains the required executable and logical game data and has passed the editor's readiness checks.

A directory merely existing on disk does not mean the variant is ready.

topics.title: Variant Manifest
topics.body:
A completed editor-owned build writes **variant-manifest.json** into the variant output. It records the baseline identity, the runtime that was built, build state, and deterministic SHA-256 identities for generated artifacts.

The manifest is diagnostic metadata. Its presence alone does not make a build Ready; always use Build Status and readiness checks.

topics.title: Interface Language
topics.body:
The interface language is independent of game text encoding, the selected translation, font profile, and active runtime variant.

English is the canonical interface language. Slovak and Czech use their own locale files and may fall back to English if a future key is not yet translated. Switching language refreshes the interface, Help, and About without changing project or game state.

topics.title: Recovery & Safety
topics.body:
Recovery & Safety verifies the captured pristine installation baseline and distinguishes editor-owned outputs from external changes.

Recovery actions are explicit. The editor may restore known mutable files from its baseline area and manage editor-owned variant directories. Unexpected external files or foreign directories are reported and preserved instead of being deleted automatically.

topics.title: What Restore Means
topics.body:
Always review the recovery preview before confirming an action.

**Restore** returns known editor-managed mutable content to its captured baseline state. **Rebuild** recreates an editor-owned variant output. **Remove owned variant** removes only an output that passes ownership checks.

Files that the editor cannot prove it owns are not silently removed. Recovery is not a substitute for manually deleting unknown files from the game directory.

topics.title: Manual Open / Legacy Import
topics.body:
Manual opening, Save As, and import remain available for compatible GAMEPC-style data and supported executable/font sources. They are compatibility tools for deliberate manual work.

For normal project work, prefer the active-variant project workflow and a controlled variant build. Opening or previewing a source should be treated as read-only until you explicitly choose a save, apply, or build action.

topics.title: Recommended Project Workflow
topics.body:
**Select installation → Select active variant → Edit project content → Check Build Status → Build variant → Review readiness/manifest → Run or Debug.**

Keep the original installation as the reference baseline. Generated runtime outputs belong to editor-owned variant builds. Text and Graphics edits are materialized by the build; saved Font and Runtime UI overrides are not materialized by Build variant in v1.0. If Recovery & Safety reports an unexpected file, investigate it before continuing.

topics.title: Troubleshooting & Known Limits
topics.body:
If a game is not available, validate the intended installation explicitly. Unsupported or altered executable layouts remain read-only unless a supported production path is available.

Replacement PNG files must preserve the image dimensions and use colors from the active 16-color palette. A PNG containing other colors must be corrected before replacement.

Character **0x81** is reserved by the engine for HUD cell erasing and is protected from normal font editing.

Some Runtime UI mappings are intentionally incomplete; those records must remain blocked rather than guessed. See the Runtime UI sections for the current limits.

topics.title: Elvira I — VGA
topics.body:
Select **Elvira I VGA / RUNVGA** as the active variant. Choose the required VGA resource, palette, and image entry, then inspect the preview before editing.

Use **Export PNG...** to create an editable copy. Preserve the original dimensions and use only colors from the active 16-color palette. **Replace PNG...** loads the edited image into the project; review the preview before saving project state or building a variant.

Do not assume that a visually similar RGB color belongs to the palette: exact palette colors are required.

topics.title: Elvira I — EGA
topics.body:
Select **Elvira I EGA / RUNEGA** before editing. The Graphics view follows the global active variant and exposes only resources that are valid for that context.

Treat VGA and EGA as separate runtime targets. Do not reuse executable names or runtime assumptions between them. Export/replace workflows must preserve the source image dimensions and the active palette constraints.

topics.title: Elvira II — VGA
topics.body:
Elvira II uses the **VGA / RUNIT** runtime profile. Select Elvira II VGA before editing graphics so the project resolves the correct game context.

Use the same controlled workflow: inspect resource and palette, export PNG, edit without changing dimensions, keep all colors inside the active 16-color palette, replace the PNG, review the preview, then save/build explicitly.

topics.title: Elvira I
topics.body:
Game Text edits compatible **GAMEPC-style** content while preserving logical string order and required non-text structure.

The **Original B**, **Translation B**, and **Difference** columns show encoded byte counts for review. They are informational; the editor must not invent an unproven fixed text-length limit.

For a translation project, work in the selected project/variant context and save deliberately. Use manual Open/Save As only when you intentionally want the legacy/manual workflow.

topics.title: Elvira II
topics.body:
Elvira II uses the same GAMEPC-style project text model with the **Elvira II VGA / RUNIT** context. Search, edit, and review encoded byte counts exactly as for Elvira I.

Keep text editing separate from Runtime UI overrides: GAMEPC text and executable-resident Runtime UI are different content sources and are built through different stages.

topics.title: Elvira I — VGA / RUNVGA
topics.body:
Runtime UI overrides are project state stored separately from GAMEPC text. Saving Runtime UI project state must not rewrite GAMEPC.

For RUNVGA, the binary routes are frozen per record (Pause.menu is PROVEN LIVE; the other listed routes are PROVEN BY BINARY), but the complete per-record production span/capacity mapping is not yet proven. Records without a proven layout remain **MappingIncomplete** and must not be patched by guesswork.

Preview and validate available records, but treat MappingIncomplete as a deliberate safety block. The grid reports proven routes as route-proven yet layout-incomplete; patching stays blocked and CompositeBuild Runtime UI override materialization is unavailable in v1.0.

topics.title: Elvira I — EGA / RUNEGA
topics.body:
RUNEGA uses its own validated Runtime UI mapping and is independent of RUNVGA. Select Elvira I EGA before reviewing or editing these records.

Runtime UI text can have fixed layout and interaction constraints. Keep translated text within the validated record capacity and preserve the original menu/hotspot behavior. Save project state first; executable changes belong to the controlled build.

topics.title: Elvira II — RUNIT
topics.body:
RUNIT Runtime UI state is separate from GAMEPC. The **SAVE_FAILURE** route has a proven production span and may be validated against its known capacity.

The exact redirected routes for **LOAD_FAILURE**, **FILE_NOT_FOUND**, and **TRY_ANOTHER_DISK** are not yet proven. Those records remain **MappingIncomplete** and must not be patched until their runtime routes are verified.

topics.title: Elvira I — VGA / RUNVGA
topics.body:
RUNVGA supports the validated extended CP852 font workflow. You can preview the source font, edit a working copy, import/export bitmap font data, or rasterize a suitable vector font into the game's 8×8 storage.

The recovered renderer displays the left 6 columns; the two rightmost stored columns are renderer-inactive. Character **0x81** is reserved for HUD erasing and is protected in every supported output path.

Create executable output only through a supported, explicit production/build action.

topics.title: Elvira I — EGA / RUNEGA
topics.body:
Elvira I EGA / RUNEGA is a supported runtime target with its own frozen Runtime UI evidence, independent of RUNVGA. RUNEGA font/CP852 mutation is NOT supported: there is no supported RUNEGA font writer or trusted mutation workflow, so do not load or apply a RUNEGA font project.

The same CP852 editing principles apply wherever a font is previewed: preserve validated storage/layout rules and keep character **0x81** reserved for the engine.

Compatibility note: RUNEGA rendering has been observed correctly in DOSBox 0.74-2 and DOSBox Staging; DOSBox-X may display different characters in some configurations.

topics.title: Elvira II — RUNIT
topics.body:
The supported RUNIT extended CP852 profile uses a validated split low/high font arrangement. Unknown or modified executable layouts remain read-only unless they match a supported production source.

Character **0x81** remains the protected HUD erase character. Edited glyphs and safe default slots are used only when an explicit supported output/build action is performed.

topics.title: Elvira I — Mods & Launcher
topics.body:
Mods & Launcher follows the selected Elvira I runtime variant. Use it to review variant readiness and configure the launcher for the intended built output.

Launcher restoration is a controlled recovery action. Do not treat manually modified or foreign launcher files as editor-owned without review.

topics.title: Elvira I — Run / Debug
topics.body:
**Run** and **Debug** require a Ready editor-owned Elvira I VGA or EGA build. Merely selecting a variant never starts a process.

Before launching, verify Build Status, readiness, and the expected executable/data output. If the build is Missing, Invalid, or Incomplete, resolve that state first.

topics.title: Elvira II — Mods & Launcher
topics.body:
Elvira II uses the VGA / RUNIT runtime profile. Configure launching only for a validated editor-owned output and review readiness before generating or updating launcher configuration.

Unknown files or foreign directories must remain outside editor ownership.

topics.title: Elvira II — Run / Debug
topics.body:
Run/Debug is available only when the Elvira II VGA build is Ready. A manifest is useful for diagnostics, but it does not authorize launch by itself.

Status refresh is read-only: it must not build, modify, or launch the game.
